proof.text:
Put A=O_E, B=O_L, t=varpi_E and v=varpi_L. Choose an A-basis e_1,...,e_d of B by [lem-sfb-local-field-integral-basis]. In the DVR B, t=u v^e with u a unit and e>=1 by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]; t has positive valuation since the coefficient absolute values are compatible. The ideals (t^n)B=(v^{en}) are cofinal with the v-powers: a compatible family at en determines its m-component by reducing any term en>=m, independently of that choice. Modulo t^n the basis identifies B/t^nB with (A/t^n)^d. These are inverse maps of constant sheaves, and inverse limits commute with the finite coordinate tuples by their universal property. Thus the actual ring map
R_W tensor_{A_W} B_W \to S_W, r tensor b |\to r b,
is an isomorphism: in the chosen basis it is the inverse-limit coordinate isomorphism R_W^d \to S_W. Multiplication agrees because the basis multiplication constants are in A, and the same constants occur in every quotient. This proves S_W=R_W tensor_{A_W}B_W as A_W-algebras, not just abstract finite freeness. The structural maps send each constant e_i to itself and commute with the quotient projections [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Hence the identification holds on both sides of f, with their specified structure maps. Tensor extension is exact since its restriction is a finite direct sum.

title: Scalar compatibility of the ordinary completed adjunction
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, the field $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, and finite coefficient fields $E\subset L$ inside $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ and chosen uniformizers [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism between finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Work on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For $B=E,L$ and $W=X,Y$, write $R_{B,W}=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{B,W}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and let $\mathcal D_{B,W}$ be the full category of derived-complete $R_{B,W}$-module complexes [def-weil-derived-complete, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $P_B=Lf^*_{\mathrm{comp},B}$ as in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], and let $F_B=Rf_{*,R_B}$ be ordinary ringed-topos derived direct image. Let
$$h_B:\operatorname{Hom}(P_BM,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(M,F_BK)$$
be the canonical completed adjunction bijection: transport the constant-coefficient completion/ordinary-adjunction composite of [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction] through [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], with right-functor identification [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison]. This fixes the bijection independently of any constructible restriction.

For $W=X,Y$, write $C_W(-)=-\otimes^L_{R_{E,W}}R_{L,W}$ for scalar extension. On complete inputs this is the strict-tower integral scalar extension under the canonical comparison of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. Use precisely the canonical comparisons of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension],
$$a:C_XP_E\xrightarrow{\sim}P_LC_Y,\qquad b:C_YF_E\xrightarrow{\sim}F_LC_X.$$
Here the normalization of these canonical comparisons is fixed as follows. Put $V_W=\operatorname{Res}_{R_{E,W}\to R_{L,W}}$, and let $\eta^c_W:1\to V_WC_W$ be the coefficient-adjunction unit $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Let $d:V_YF_L\xrightarrow{\sim}F_EV_X$ be the comparison of the two ringed-topos factorizations [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. The map $b_K$ is the coefficient-adjunction transpose of
$$F_EK\xrightarrow{F_E(\eta^c_{X,K})}F_EV_XC_XK\xrightarrow{d_{C_XK}^{-1}}V_YF_LC_XK.$$
The map $a$ is ordinary pullback/tensor reassociation followed by the unit-compatible completion comparison. All coefficient associators here and in the common-stage construction are the balanced tensor maps $((x\otimes s)\otimes t)\mapsto x\otimes st$, transported by the specified $\chi$ comparisons [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition].
The bijections $h_B$ and their inverses are $\mathcal O_B$-linear. For $M\in\mathcal D_{E,Y}$, $K\in\mathcal D_{E,X}$, $u:P_EM\to K$ and $v:M\to F_EK$, one has
$$h_L\bigl(C_X(u)\circ a_M^{-1}\bigr)=b_K\circ C_Y\bigl(h_E(u)\bigr),$$
$$h_L^{-1}\bigl(b_K\circ C_Y(v)\bigr)=C_X\bigl(h_E^{-1}(v)\bigr)\circ a_M^{-1}.$$
These equalities use the given tensor/completion and ringed-topos comparisons, and respect identity extensions and towers $E\subset L\subset L'$ under their tensor associators. On bounded constructible objects [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], raw scalar localization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] gives the same equalities for the localized bijections and rational scalar extension. Consequently, for the common finite-stage Hom sets of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], taking the $h_B$-adjunct or inverse adjunct of a representative is independent of the common finite coefficient field and of the representative.
